newsitem.title: ITALY: Dealers puzzle over high Olivetti share trade.
newsitem.headline: Dealers puzzle over high Olivetti share trade.

text.p: Turnover of shares in Italy's Olivetti group has soared since events at the company took a turn for the worse more than two weeks ago and the share price began to tumble, prompting dealers to wonder who is buying.

Brokers say volume on Olivetti on an average day ranges from between five to 10 million shares but figures from Milan's stock market council show since September 3, when Olivetti's troubles hotted up, daily volume has held above 20 million shares.
Traders, asked whether a single buyer could be amassing shares, said it was hard to identify any individual buyer, with small orders coming in from lots of different stockbrokers.

"There's no one in particular on the buy side. There are high volumes with a high amount of proposals (for trades) put into the market so you can't spot anyone in particular," one broker here said, noting the small size of many of the trades.
Traders say some of the selling early in the crisis came from institutional investors ridding themselves of the stock.
But another broker said, "I have thought for the last couple of days that something could be going on. Even if you take into account speculators, somebody has got to be buying the shares."

Turnover hit 81.88 million shares on September 4, the day which bore the reaction of the market to chairman Carlo De Benedetti's sudden resignation and a 1996 first half loss of 440.2 billion lire announced late on September 3.
Activity for September 4 also contained the resignation of Olivetti former director general Renzo Francesconi, who quit saying he did not agree with the half-year accounts for 1996.
Olivetti shares were then suspended from trade for September 5 and 6 by market watchdog Consob as it tried to get to the bottom of Francesconi's comments.
The following Monday turnover was 54 million and on Tuesday 88.51 million, with 69.33 million, 40.75 million and 23.04 million for the subsequent two days.

Stock market data show between September 2 and 16 more than 364 million shares changed hands to the order of 233 billion lire. Since then daily volume has been 33 to 50 million shares and rose to 71 million on Thursday.
